# Message delivery standard (MD-01..MD-08)

Status: ACTIVE (2026-11-02). Applies to any runtime that delivers a message a
model wrote to a human channel: a chat reply, a comment, a review thread.

`agent-notification.md` governs whether a message may be sent at all, to whom,
and in how many sentences (NT-01..NT-10). This standard governs the handover: how
the message becomes a durable record, how the transport is called, what may be
claimed afterwards, and how the runtime behaves when the channel refuses. A
runtime that sends first and records later has no answer to any of those
questions after a crash.

Evidence: `../docs/knowledge-base/superagent-prototype-2026-11.md` (mechanism
table M6: durable receipt, domain-derived message id, transport dedupe, three
delivery facts). The general effect machinery is `durable-effects.md`
(EF-01..EF-10); a message is one effect kind on that queue, with a human channel
as its transport.

## MD-01 -- Write the guarantee down, and never claim exactly-once

The runtime MUST state its delivery guarantee in the documentation that owns the
channel, using all three parts:

| Guarantee | Scope | Where it is enforced |
|---|---|---|
| At most one queued message per originating event per session | The receipt | The receipt key includes the unit and the event id (MD-07) |
| At least one delivery attempt per channel for a queued message, unless it is withdrawn (MD-05) | The transport | The queue retries until a terminal answer (EF-05) |
| Duplicates, if any, are collapsed by the message id | The transport | The transport receives the receipt's message id and deduplicates on it (MD-02) |

The runtime MUST NOT claim exactly-once delivery. A crash between the transport
call and the completion write leaves the acknowledgement unknown, so the only
honest claims are at-least-once execution and a dedupe key, and exactly-once is a
property of the pair rather than of one call.

The session bounds the claim, not the identity: a retry in a later session
reuses the same receipt and therefore the same message id, so the per-session
statement is a weaker restatement of the key's rule, never a licence to send
again. A guarantee stated without its scope is not a guarantee: "we do not
duplicate messages" is false the moment a retry happens on a transport that does
not deduplicate, and the documentation MUST say which transport has which
property.

## MD-02 -- Durable receipt first, transport second

Delivery has two phases and their order is fixed. First the runtime commits a
receipt: message id, unit, conversation, originating event id, payload, channel,
and the time the receipt was made. Only then does it call the transport, passing
the message id as the dedupe key.

- The message id is generated by the receipt from domain facts under EF-03. It is
  stable across attempts, and a transport retry reuses it rather than minting a
  new one.
- A transport call whose receipt did not commit MUST NOT happen. An
  acknowledgement with no receipt cannot be reconciled after a crash and cannot
  be deduplicated.
- The transport MUST deduplicate by that id. A channel that cannot deduplicate is
  named in the guarantee (MD-01), with the consequence that a retry can produce
  a visible duplicate there; the runtime does not pretend the missing property
  exists.
- The receipt is the only durable home of the delivery facts. There is no
  process-local outbox and no second table; message state is derived from the
  receipt when asked (VI-15).

A receipt row is not a claim that anything was sent. It is the record that the
runtime committed to try, which is what makes the retry safe and the report
truthful.

## MD-03 -- Ordering belongs to (unit, conversation)

Messages carry an ordering key of `(unit, conversation)`. A later message of the
same unit waits behind an earlier unsent message of that unit, and a message of
another unit never waits, even when both target the same conversation or the same
channel.

The unit is in the key because a unit's narrative must not overtake itself: a
follow-up that says "the fix is ready" before the message that says "I started"
confuses the reader and the record. The conversation is in the key because the
same unit may report in two threads whose order is independent. The channel is
deliberately not in the key: two units sharing a channel are independent
writers, and serializing them would let one slow unit delay every other.

The mechanics are EF-06. A withdrawn head settles as dropped (MD-05) and a
permanently failed head settles as failed (EF-07); either way the next message of
that stream proceeds, and a head that is merely deferred blocks its own stream
only.

## MD-04 -- Classify the transport answer, close the permanent set

Every transport answer MUST be classified, and the permanent class is a closed
set of `gone` conditions: the channel was deleted, the thread was locked, the bot
was removed from the space, or the recipient identity no longer exists. Each
condition has a code, and it is terminal for this message (EF-07).

Everything else is retryable. An error that matches no declared condition MUST be
recorded as retryable with its raw name and message, and the record MUST keep
that name; it MUST NOT be guessed into `gone`. Guessing permanent drops a
message a later retry would have delivered, and the guess is invisible after the
fact because the record carries only the guess.

The closed set is versioned with the channel kind. Adding a condition requires
evidence that retrying it cannot succeed, plus a test that the condition routes
to a terminal outcome. A transport that returns a bare status code with no
classification is retryable by default until its code is documented, and the
unclassified code is named in the failure record so the next reader can close it.

## MD-05 -- Withdraw and settle, and let the receipt own the state

A message withdrawn before dispatch MUST settle as dropped without a transport
call. A message withdrawn while a send is in flight MUST settle as dropped as
well, and it MUST NOT re-queue. Withdrawal is a fact about the request, not a
promise about the network: the transport call may already have reached the
channel, so the runtime records the drop and does not retry it.

If the transport later confirms that the withdrawn message arrived, the receipt
records the delivery as a separate fact beside the drop. It does not revive the
message, does not re-send it, and does not rewrite the drop into a send. The two
facts describe two different things that happened, and both stay visible.

The receipt is the only durable place these facts live. A caller-side flag, a
cache entry, or an in-memory set of withdrawn ids does not survive the process
and cannot be reconciled after a restart. A dropped message is never re-sent by a
retry sweep, a restart, or a fallback to another channel; a fallback would be a
second message about the same event and violates MD-07.

## MD-06 -- A queued message is not a sent message

The runtime reports the transport state, never the intent. Until the transport
answers, the accurate words are queued or sending. After a permanent answer or a
withdrawal, the accurate word is dropped or failed, with the reason code. After
an acknowledgement, the accurate word is sent, with the channel and the time of
the acknowledgement.

A model's own sentence that it sent something is a claim about its intent, not
evidence about the channel, and it MUST NOT be promoted into the record. A queued
message reported as sent is the most damaging version of this error because the
human acts on it: they look for a comment that does not exist, or they stop
waiting for one that will arrive.

The reported state is derived from the receipt facts (VI-15), and a dropped
message is reported as dropped even when the drop was intentional. Terminal
honesty is the notification standard's rule (NT-09); this standard supplies the
facts that make it possible.

## MD-07 -- Deduplicate by the originating event, not by text

Every message MUST carry the event id that caused it, and that id is part of the
receipt key together with the unit (MD-02). The same event retried produces one
message: the second attempt coalesces onto the existing receipt under EF-04
instead of queueing a second one.

A reworded message about the same event MUST NOT silently queue a second one.
While the first message is unsent, the reword coalesces as a new generation
(EF-04) and the transport sends the latest text once. After the first message is
sent, dropped, or permanently failed, the runtime refuses the reword and returns
the existing message id with its state, so the writer can decide whether the
situation calls for a genuinely new message with a new event id.

Text comparison is not deduplication. A reword evades it, two different events
that happen to share a sentence collide under it, and neither failure is
observable in the record. The event is the identity; the text is payload.

## MD-08 -- Payload limits are transport facts

The runtime MUST measure the payload once, before queueing, in a unit named by
the transport: words for a human-facing notification ceiling (NT-04 owns the
ceiling), UTF-8 bytes for an API body limit, or characters for a field limit.
The unit is stored with the channel configuration and is used for every message
of that kind; mixing units turns a passing measurement into a failing one.

The runtime MUST refuse at the boundary. A payload over the named maximum
returns a permanent `payload_too_large` result carrying the measured value, the
limit, and the unit, and the message is not queued. Refusal is a fact the writer
can act on; a truncation is a silent edit of what a person will read.

The runtime MUST NOT truncate silently and MUST NOT split a message into parts to
evade a limit. A split changes the number of messages a human receives, defeats
the sentence ceiling (NT-04), and turns one receipt into several, none of which
is the message the model wrote. The limit belongs to the transport, not to the
model: a prompt instruction is advisory (WA-11), while the queue's measurement
and refusal are enforced.

## Rejected alternatives

| Rejected | Why |
|---|---|
| Send first, record the receipt afterwards | A crash after the send leaves no receipt and no dedupe key, so the retry duplicates and the drop is unknowable |
| Retry loops inside the calling request | The retries die with the request, block the caller's thread, and leave no durable attempt count for the next process |
| Length limits enforced by the model in the prompt | Prompt text is advisory and the model can misjudge units; only the queue can measure the payload and refuse it |
| Deduplicating by message text | A reword evades the check, and two different events that share a sentence collide under it |
| Storing delivery state in a process-local outbox | The process is the thing that dies; the receipt must survive it |
